sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Camas, WA?
sections.html:
Camas is a Clark County city on the Columbia River, about 20 miles northeast of Portland, with Vancouver on its west side and Washougal on its east. The Census Bureau estimates 27,749 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 6.0 percent from the April 2020 estimates base. Households here are large and incomes are high, and county-level steps run through Clark County offices.

The city was incorporated on June 18, 1906, and takes its name from the camas lily. A paper mill opened in 1883 and shaped the town for more than a century. The mill sits at the west end of downtown and passed to Georgia-Pacific in 2000 and to Koch Industries in 2005. In 2018 Koch announced plans to lay off roughly 200 to 300 workers, and technology employers such as Analog Devices and TSMC Washington now share the local job base.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Camas homes and households?
sections.html:
Camas owner-occupied homes have a median value of $711,700, and 78.3 percent of housing is owner-occupied, per Census Bureau QuickFacts. Values marked 2020-2024 come from the American Community Survey.

Nearly four of five Camas homes are owner-occupied, and households average close to three people. Buyers here are typically families, so bedrooms, yards and school boundaries get close attention.

sections.h2: How do the Camas layout and schools affect a sale?
sections.html:
Lakes, creeks and Prune Hill shape what buyers see in Camas. Prune Hill, an extinct volcanic vent, rises in the middle of town, and Lacamas Lake, Round Lake, Lacamas Creek, the Washougal River and the Columbia River all lie inside city limits. Lacamas Park runs along State Route 500 with trails around the lakes, and a long list of city parks is scattered through the neighborhoods.

  • Downtown Camas: the historic core near the mill, with the Liberty Theatre and the festival calendar, including Camas Days.
  • Prune Hill: a hillside residential area with a sports park named for it.
  • Lacamas Lake and Round Lake: lakeside homes next to park trails and boat launches.
  • Grass Valley and Forest Home: areas with city parks of the same names.

Most of Camas belongs to the Camas School District. Small parts of the city lie inside Evergreen Public Schools, so check the district for the address on any listing. Demolition plans for the paper mill have proceeded, with work expected to finish by 2027, and the site is expected to become waterfront on Camas Slough as an extension of the downtown district. Buyers who ask about the neighborhood's direction will likely ask about that project.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Camas house that has an ADU or extra units?
sections.html:
Camas adopted Ordinance 25-025 in 2025 to align with new state housing rules. An accessory dwelling unit is a unit up to 1,000 square feet, attached, detached or a mix, and a lot can have up to two. Camas also allows two middle housing units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable, and it created a unit lot subdivision process that lets parent lots divide into separately owned child lots.

These rules can add value, and they create questions for sellers. ADUs count toward the middle housing total, so a lot with one main home can add two ADUs, while a lot that already holds two middle housing units cannot. Before you list, confirm what was permitted.

  • Ask the Camas Community Development Department, which has Planning, Development Engineering and Building divisions, for permit history on garage conversions, basements and additions.
  • Permits and inspections run through the city's online system, which has taken applications, inspection requests and status tracking since June 12, 2024.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Camas house fast?
sections.html:
Camas listings tend to be move-in ready and well kept, so a house that needs work stands out. Sellers who need speed generally choose from these options:

  • Prepare and list: repairs, staging and a few weeks of showings, with the strongest price when the home is in good shape.
  • Sell as-is to an investor or cash buyer: useful for deferred maintenance, estate sales, vacant houses and tenant matters, with a closing date you set.
  • Negotiate a leaseback or delayed possession: helpful when you need time to move after closing.

Ask any buyer for proof of funds and a plain written offer. Then compare the net proceeds, not only the price: the excise tax, payoff of any loan and prorated property taxes all come off the top.

sections.h2: What excise tax and paperwork apply to a Camas sale?
sections.html:
For a deeded transfer in Washington, the excise tax affidavit, the deed and payment go to the county treasurer where the property sits, which for Camas is the Clark County Treasurer. The Department of Revenue says only one exemption can be claimed per transfer and that records must be kept for at least four years. If you overpay, a refund request must be filed within four years of the sale.

The state rate is graduated: 1.1 percent on the portion of the price up to $525,000, 1.28 percent from there to $1,525,000, then higher tiers above that. At $711,700, the Camas median owner-occupied value, the state tax on a sale would be about $8,165 before the local add-on: about $5,775 on the first $525,000 plus about $2,390 on the rest. Treat that as an illustration and ask the escrow officer for the exact bill.

Washington also requires a seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020, delivered within five business days of mutual acceptance unless otherwise agreed. The form covers title, water, sewer, structural and other topics, and the seller is told to sign and date each page. Camas houses near lakes, creeks or slopes should have drainage and septic or sewer details ready, since those questions appear on the form.

sections.h2: How do Clark County property taxes work for a Camas seller?
sections.html:
Clark County collects real property tax in two halves, due April 30 and October 31. The Treasurer says first-half statements are available by March 15 and second-half statements typically by September 15. The second-half 2026 date has passed, and the next due date is April 30, 2027.

For 2023 and later years, late taxes on a residential parcel with four or fewer units accrue 0.75 percent interest per month, with no penalties. The Treasurer accepts mailed payments only if the envelope is postmarked by the due date, and it does not currently accept prepayment of future-year taxes, with exceptions for certain sale transactions such as personal property and mobile homes. Call 564.397.2252 or email treasoff@clark.wa.gov, and ask about the county's tax relief programs for homeowners who meet eligibility requirements.

faqs.q: How many people live in Camas, WA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 27,749 residents as of July 1, 2025, compared with 26,065 in the 2020 census and 19,355 in 2010.

faqs.q: How many ADUs can I build on a Camas lot?
faqs.a: Up to two. Camas defines an ADU as a unit up to 1,000 square feet, attached or detached. ADUs count toward the middle housing allowance, which is two units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half or full year, and October 31 for the second half. Mailed payments need a postmark on or before the due date. Late residential taxes for four or fewer units accrue 0.75 percent per month.

faqs.q: Who collects the excise tax on a Camas home sale?
faqs.a: The county treasurer where the property is located, which for Camas is Clark County. The seller usually pays. The affidavit, deed and payment are submitted together for a deeded transfer.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Camas homes?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Camas School District. Small parts of the city limits fall inside Evergreen Public Schools, so confirm the district for the exact address.
